page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.small is an entry-level shared-core virtual machine instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 1 shared vCPU mapping to 1 physical core and thread, accompanied by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. It comes equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio.

Hardware capabilities include support for instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES cryptography, and BMI2. The instance contains zero dedicated GPUs and includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for file systems and data persistence. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 0 Gbps without bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses, indicating reliance on shared host network capacity.

Synthetic benchmarks reflect its single shared-core allocation and position the instance within the lowest comparative tiers. Stress-ng scores reached 1072.5 for both single-core and multi-core evaluations. Geekbench tests yielded 791.0 in single-core and 890.0 in multi-core metrics, with specific tasks like Clang compilation measuring 896.0 and text processing measuring 848.0. PassMark assessments registered a CPU score of 1259.2 and a memory score of 803.96, while uncached memory throughput reached 8.56 GB/s for read and 7.08 GB/s for write operations.

Given the shared vCPU design and modest compute output, ecs.mn4.small offers an economical footprint for lightweight, non-critical background jobs, small testing environments, low-traffic internal web services, and lightweight utility microservices that do not demand sustained compute performance or high local I/O throughput.
